taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes A. vagrans was formerly included in A. ferreus (clouded salamander); some of the Vancouver Island populations are believed by some authors to derive from human-mediated introductions, though the Canadian management plan considers a natural origin better supported.
fieldMarks: Slender salamander with light grey or bronze mottling over a brown to greyish-black head, back and tail.
Adults 75-130 mm total length (50-76 mm snout-vent), weighing 1.5-5.6 g.
Squared-off toes and no constriction at the base of the tail separate it from other lungless salamanders in British Columbia.
Juveniles have a bronze dorsal stripe and a bronze patch on the head and snout that fade with age; adult colour is reached at about 45 mm snout-vent.
behavior: Terrestrial and probably nocturnal; moves short distances (94% of recaptures within 10 m) and estivates deep in logs and moist crevices in dry periods.
Lives in and on large decaying logs and bark, and in old-growth forest canopy; on seabird islands it uses drift logs and burrows.
Eggs (3-28) are laid in a gelatinous cluster under bark or in a rotting log; females guard nests and young hatch as miniature adults.
Feeds on small arthropods such as ants, beetles, spiders, isopods and mites.
habitat: Moist forest (Douglas-fir, redwood, hardwood-conifer) in humid coastal areas, using logs, bark, talus and rock crevices for refuge and breeding.
Needs large, mid-decay down logs with sloughing bark.
range: Humid coastal forests of northern California (Del Norte to Sonoma County) and, in Canada, Vancouver Island, adjacent small islands and one Sunshine Coast location in British Columbia; absent from Oregon and Washington.

lookalikes.name: Clouded salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Formerly treated as the same species (A. ferreus); the sources read give no simple field mark, so locality and expert identification are the guides.
